name: minimal-backend-api
title: Minimal Backend API Implementation
description: Add a new backend API endpoint with minimal implementation principles and dependency budget constraints. Focuses on solving the immediate need without over-engineering.

principles: YAGNI - You Ain't Gonna Need It
Prefer boring solutions over clever ones
forbiddenPatterns: plugin system for single use case

planner.description: Defines the minimal scope needed to solve the problem. Identifies what NOT to build.

executor.description: Implements only what's required. Resists the urge to add nice-to-haves.

reviewer.description: Reviews for over-engineering: abstractions without multiple uses, dependencies without justification, code solving problems not yet proven to exist.

steps.task: Read the feature request and define the minimal scope: what input, what output, what error cases must be handled NOW. List non-goals explicitly. Verify dependency budget allows the planned approach. Output JSON with scope, acceptance, non-goals, and budget check.

principles: Start with the simplest thing that could work

steps.task: Implement the minimal scope. Inline simple logic. Use existing utilities. Add one dependency only if stdlib/existing code cannot solve it. Write tests for the happy path and documented error cases only. No abstractions unless there are 3+ call sites.
Run syntax check and tests. Fix failures. Verify no unplanned dependencies were added. Output JSON with test results, files changed, dependencies added, and readiness.

Review for over-engineering. Check: Are there abstractions with single call sites? Dependencies without clear justification? Code solving future problems? Configuration for things that don't vary? Reply PASS if minimal or list specific over-engineering with file:line evidence.
